What

What Land Clearing Actually Involves

Clearing a parcel isn't just knocking down trees. Here's what a proper Roubic clearing looks like from boundary walk to final grade.

Land clearing is the systematic clearing of multiple trees, brush, and understory from a parcel. Roubic works two ways. Full clearing removes all vegetation — trees, brush, undergrowth — and hauls the debris off-site, leaving the parcel ready for construction or pasture conversion. Selective clearing preserves marked trees while removing the rest, so a homeowner can expand usable yard while keeping mature canopy. Lot clearing is the build-site-specific variant; brush clearing targets overgrown understory without the large trees. Every variant follows the same process, scaled to the size of the job.

Why

Why NE Ohio Property Owners Need Clearing

The most common clearing drivers we see across Cuyahoga and Geauga counties — practical, recurring reasons, not theoretical ones. Every one of these shows up regularly on the parcels Aaron walks.

  • New-construction lot prepBuild-site prep for homes, additions, driveways, outbuildings, and pool installations — the parcel has to be cleared and graded first.
  • Overgrown parcels resetLand that has gone untended for years and needs to be reset for use, sale, or maintenance before it can serve any purpose.
  • Invasive-species understoryMultiflora rose, honeysuckle, Callery pear, and garlic mustard degrade native ground and drop property value the longer they spread.
  • Brush + wildfire riskAccumulated brush becomes a real fire hazard in dry stretches — clearing it back removes the fuel load close to structures.

How

How Roubic Approaches Every Clearing

The same 8-step process on a 1-acre suburban lot prep or a 5+ acre rural Geauga parcel. It's the reason customers hand us the whole job — clearing, grinding, and grade — under one contract.

1

Site Walk + Boundary Verification

We establish exactly what's in scope and what stays preserved, walking the boundary with the customer.

2

John Deere skid steer, track loader, Bandit chipper, and dump trailers staged on site.

Working outside-in and keeping a staging pad for orderly debris management.

Included in the full-clear contract — stumps ground below grade, not left behind.

7

Debris hauled to a licensed disposal facility, or chips dropped on-site if you want them.

8

Final-Grade Pass

A box-blade grade pass leaves the parcel construction-ready or pasture-ready.

What If You Wait

The Cost of Letting a Parcel Go Overgrown

Every one of these is a recurring, measurable consequence we see on parcels across Cuyahoga and Geauga counties.

Reduced Property Value

Overgrown parcels measurably reduce property value — buyers assume the worst about the underlying conditions they can't see.

Wildlife Pressure

Ticks, rodents, and sometimes coyotes move in as a parcel reverts to brush and becomes cover for them.

Wildfire Risk

Accumulated brush and dead understory spike fire risk during dry seasons, right up against structures.

Construction Delays

Build timelines slip when clearing is held until the last minute instead of scheduled ahead of the crew.

Invasive Spread

Invasive species established in an overgrown understory get far more expensive to remediate once they spread.

Nuisance Ordinances

In some Geauga townships, severely overgrown parcels violate nuisance ordinances and can trigger municipal action.

Common Clearing Questions

Land Clearing FAQ

Seven answers before you book — straight from Aaron's actual clearing estimate conversations.

How much does land clearing cost per acre in Ohio?
Land clearing in NE Ohio runs $1,500–$20,000+ per acre depending on density. Light brush is $1,500–$3,000/acre; medium-density wooded lots are $3,000–$5,000/acre; heavy mature wooded lots can exceed $20,000/acre with full haul-off. Selective clearing (preserving marked trees) typically costs more than full clearing. See the Tree Service Cost Guide for additional context.
Do I need a permit to clear my land in Geauga County?
Geauga County generally follows standard private-property rules — no routine permit for clearing on private residential property. However, large-scale clearing that changes land use (residential to agricultural, agricultural to commercial) may trigger a zoning review at the township level. Wetland delineation may apply near streams or seasonal water features. Roubic confirms permit and zoning requirements as part of every clearing estimate.
What's the difference between brush clearing and full land clearing?
Brush clearing targets the understory — small-diameter trees (under about 6 inches DBH), saplings, vines, and invasive shrubs — without removing mature canopy trees. Full land clearing removes everything, including stumps, with final grading. Brush clearing is faster and cheaper; full clearing prepares the site for construction or major land-use change.
Can you clear land in winter?
Yes — winter is often the best time to clear in NE Ohio. Frozen ground minimizes soil compaction and rut damage from heavy equipment, and leaves-off visibility makes boundary markers and preserved trees much easier to see. We clear from October through March routinely. Spring and wet conditions are poor timing because of equipment ruts.
Do you offer forestry mulching?
No — Roubic does not currently offer forestry mulching as a clearing method. Our land clearing service uses traditional cut-and-haul or selective clearing approaches with skid steer, track loader, and chipper equipment. If forestry mulching is specifically required for your project, we can recommend a partner contractor who specializes in that method.
How long does land clearing take?
Light brush on a 1-acre lot: typically 1–2 days. Medium-density 1–2 acre lots: 2–4 days. Heavy wooded 1-acre lots: 3–5 days, sometimes longer with haul-off. Multi-acre clearing scales roughly linearly. Permit timelines (when applicable) can add 2–6 weeks to the start date.
Does clearing include stump grinding and debris haul-off?
On a full clear, yes — below-grade stump grinding is included in the contract, and debris is hauled off to a licensed disposal facility as the standard finish. If you'd rather keep the chips, we drop them on-site instead. Either way it's coordinated with a final-grade pass under one contract, so you're not booking clearing, grinding, and grade as three separate mobilizations.
